//: The default configuration opens one PR per dependency, which is wrong for
this repository in a specific and demonstrable way: a bot bumped the
Compose compiler on its own and broke the Android build, because that
version is only meaningful in a pair with Kotlin.
e: This version (1.5.15) of the Compose Compiler requires Kotlin version
1.9.25 but you appear to be using Kotlin version 1.9.24
So: anything that must move together is grouped, and anything that cannot
be verified by CI is left for a person.

packageRules.description: Kotlin and the Compose compiler plugin are released together and only work together. Never separately, ever.
The AndroidX stack moves as a set. compose-bom exists precisely to keep these in step, so bumping one at a time defeats the point of it.
AGP and Gradle have a supported-version matrix. A new AGP frequently requires a newer Gradle, so they arrive together or the build fails on the first one.
A major version of the build toolchain changes behaviour rather than versions. CI can prove the app still compiles, but not that it still behaves, so these wait for a person.
compileSdk is not a dependency — raising it opts into new platform behaviour and needs the matching SDK installed on every builder. Renovate cannot know when that is true.
Actions are grouped and automerged on patch/minor: they are covered by every workflow run, so a break is visible immediately and revertible in one click.
Node's major version in CI is a real change of runtime. The engines floor in package.json is a compatibility claim and is not Renovate's to move.
Dev-only type checking. Grouped because @types/node and typescript are only meaningful against each other.
wrangler is the deploy tool for the coordinator; a major version can change wrangler.toml's schema.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: A security fix does not wait for Monday.
